$comment: Pairings that already failed the contrast gate when it landed
(YaleSites-Internal#1632). The gate ignores exactly these and nothing else,
so any NEW failure breaks the build immediately.
This is a burn-down list, not an opt-out. contrast-gate.test.mjs enforces
both directions: an entry that starts passing must be deleted, and an entry
whose pairing no longer exists must be deleted. Adding an entry to turn a
red build green is not a fix -- fix the colors.

leakCase.reason: A section's foreground inheriting onto a block's background, for every (global theme x section theme x block theme) combination. NOT an approved pairing and NOT gated per-pairing -- it is what happens when a component paints a background without publishing a foreground, and Phase 2 owns the surface contract that fixes it. What IS enforced is that the number cannot get worse: a palette or theme change that pushed more combinations below AA would otherwise go unnoticed until #1631 got there.

section/seven/three/border.reason: --color-layout-border was deliberately left alone by the #1613 audit: it is not only a border colour, the CTA atom draws its filled-button background from it, so re-pointing it changes buttons as well as borders.

section/seven/four/border.reason: Same --color-layout-border exclusion as section/seven/three/border, and the closest of the two to the line -- 2.99:1 against a 3:1 minimum.

cta/any/three/text.reason: button-cta-themes.three publishes its own background/text pair and that pair fails AA normal text. Fixing it is a palette decision for a designer, not something this gate should make unilaterally, so it lands baselined and flagged rather than silently unchecked.

cta/any/four/text.reason: Same as cta/any/three/text and considerably worse -- 1.73:1 is close to invisible. Needs a designer to re-pick either the background or the text colour for button-cta-themes.four.

safe-slot/two/slot-three/slot-one.reason: #1539's safe-foreground rule was derived against slot-nine only, so it does not hold on section theme six's slot-three background. #1613's audit already said as much in prose; the gate is where it becomes visible.

safe-slot/two/slot-three/slot-six.reason: As safe-slot/two/slot-three/slot-one, and only just short at 4.32:1 -- a small palette adjustment would clear it.

safe-slot/five/slot-three/slot-one.reason: As safe-slot/two/slot-three/slot-one, in global theme five. slot-one and slot-six are the same colour in this theme, so the two entries move together.

safe-slot/five/slot-three/slot-six.reason: As safe-slot/five/slot-three/slot-one -- same measured ratio because the theme points both slots at the same colour.

safe-slot/seven/slot-three/slot-one.reason: As safe-slot/two/slot-three/slot-one, in global theme seven.

safe-slot/seven/slot-four/slot-one.reason: The only #1539 failure on a background other than slot-three: global theme seven pairs a pale slot-four with a slot-one that is not dark enough to carry normal text on it.
